questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘Customise’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Personalise'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Customise"** refers to** modifying or configuring something to suit a particular individual or task. **
 
• **Customisation** involves tailoring features, settings, or options based on specific user preferences.
 
• **Personalisation** is a **direct synonym as it refers to creating a tailored experience for the use**r.
 
• **Personalising** something means adapting it to meet individual needs or desires.
 
• In the context of the passage, new media allows users** to personalise** their experience by adjusting settings or content as per their liking.

Therefore, **"personalise" accurately captures the essence of creating a unique, user-specific configuration.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Realise: **This means to become aware of or to make something real, which is unrelated to **customisation.**
 
• **Generalise:** This means to make something more widespread or common, the opposite of **customising.**
 
• **Ritualised:** This means to make something into a ritual or habit, which does not imply any tailoring or** personalisation.**

questions.question: Why is it not easy to draw a line between old media and new media?

options.text: Because new media can be customised to users’ preferences
Because new media is considered to be the multimedia and digital form of communication
Because both include various kinds of medium
Because old media has found new ways of representation in digital forms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Explanation:** The statement discusses** the difficulty in drawing a clear line between old media and new media.**
 
• This is** primarily** because old media has adapted to** the digital age **by finding new ways of representation in digital formats.
 
• This **evolution blurs the distinction between old and new media, making it challenging to categorize them separately.**
 
• This aligns with** option 4**, which states** that old media has found new ways of representation in digital forms.**
 
• In summary,** option 4 best explains the reason for the difficulty in distinguishing between old and new media** by highlighting how old media has adapted to digital forms. Options 1, 2, and 3 either describe features of new media or general characteristics that do not directly address the core issue.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Because new media can be customised to users’ preferences:** While it is true that new media offers customization, this feature does not explain the difficulty in distinguishing between old and new media.
 
• **Because new media is considered to be the multimedia and digital form of communication:** This option describes what new media is but does not address why it is difficult to differentiate it from old media.
 
• **Because both include various kinds of medium:** Although both old and new media encompass various forms of media, this fact alone does not explain the challenge in drawing a line between them.

questions.question: How does the passage distinguish new media from old media?

options.text: New media includes user interaction, whereas, through old media, we only consume information.
New media increases screen time and could be addictive and unhealthy, unlike old media.
New media is fast and digitally based, whereas old media has never been beyond the conventional methods of representation.
New media caters to a larger audience and is more popular than old media.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Explanation:** The passage **distinguishes new media from old media by highlighting the interactive nature of new media.**
 
• It** emphasizes **that new media** allows for user interaction, enabling individuals to engage with and contribute to the content.**
 
• In contrast,** old media** is characterized by a **one-way flow of information **where users are primarily **consumers of content **without the ability to interact or contribute.
 
• This distinction aligns with** option 1**, which correctly **states that new media includes user interaction, whereas old media is limited to information consumption.**
 
• In summary, **option 1 **best captures the primary distinction made in the passage between new and old media, emphasizing the interactive nature of new media compared to the consumption-focused nature of old media. **Options 2, 3, and 4 **either address different aspects or do not align with the main point of the passage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **New media increases screen time and could be addictive and unhealthy, unlike old media:** While this statement might be true, it does not directly address the primary distinction made in the passage regarding the interactive nature of new media versus the consumption-focused nature of old media.

 
 
• **New media is fast and digitally based, whereas old media has never been beyond the conventional methods of representation:** This statement highlights the technological differences between new and old media but does not focus on the key aspect of user interaction versus information consumption, which is the main distinction discussed in the passage.
 
• **New media caters to a larger audience and is more popular than old media:** Popularity and audience reach are not the central themes of the passage's distinction between new and old media. The passage focuses on the nature of interaction and consumption, not on audience size or popularity.

questions.question: What does the term ‘Catch-all’ mean?

__
 
• The term** "catch-all" **is typically used **to describe a category or term that encompasses a wide variety of items or concepts. **
 
• In the passage, **"new media"** is described **as a catch-all term for various types of electronic communications**.
 
• This implies that** "new media" **includes **a broad range of media forms without being limited to a specific type**.
 
• **The term does not specify any particular type of media, source of information, or source of entertainment, but rather includes all possible variations.**

questions.question: Select an appropriate title for the passage.

options.text: The History of the Human Mind
The Role of the Human Mind in Promoting Positive Change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'The Power of Creativity'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate title for the passage is: **The Power of Creativity.**
 
• This **title** accurately reflects the central theme of the passage,** which discusses the multifaceted nature of creativity, its impact on individuals and society, and its role in bringing about positive change. **
 
• The passage explores **various aspects of creativity, including its definition, theories, manifestations, challenges, and historical significance.** Additionally, the passage emphasizes **the importance of creativity in addressing social, political, and environmental challenges throughout history.**
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 2) The Complexities of Human Cognition** focuses more on the broader topic of human cognition, which is discussed in the passage but is not the primary focus. While the passage touches upon the intricacies of the human mind, it places greater emphasis on creativity as a specific aspect of human cognition.
 
• **Option 3) The History of the Human Mind** is too narrow in scope and does not encompass the full range of topics discussed in the passage. While the passage briefly mentions the historical study of the human mind, it primarily focuses on creativity and its various dimensions.
 
• **Option 4) The Role of the Human Mind in Promoting Positive Change **is too specific and does not capture the breadth of topics covered in the passage. While the passage does discuss the role of creativity in promoting positive change, it also explores other aspects of creativity, such as its definition, manifestations, and challenges. Therefore, this title does not fully encapsulate the content of the passage.

questions.question: What is the main focus of the passage?

options.text: The complexities and challenges of cognitive processes.
The mysteries of the human mind.
The nature of creativity, its benefits and challenges.
The nature of fancy and imagination.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The nature of creativity, its benefits and challenges.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The main focus of the passage is:** The nature of creativity, its benefits and challenges.**
 
• Explanation: The **passage primarily discusses the concept of creativity, exploring its definition, theories, manifestations, and significance.** It delves into the process of creativity, various theories proposed to explain it, and its multifaceted nature.
 
• Additionally, the passage **examines the benefits of creativity, such as its potential to bring about positive change in the world**, as well as the challenges associated with creative expression, including self-doubt, external pressures, and rejection.
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1)** **The complexities and challenges of cognitive processes:** While the passage touches upon cognitive processes, such as imagination and problem-solving, its primary focus is on creativity rather than on broader cognitive processes.
 
• **Option 2)** **The mysteries of the human mind:** While the passage discusses the human mind and its ability to create and imagine, it primarily focuses on creativity as a specific aspect of the human mind, rather than on the broader mysteries of the human mind.
 
• **Option 4)** **The nature of fancy and imagination:** While the passage mentions the human mind's capacity to create and imagine, it goes beyond mere fancy and imagination to explore the concept of creativity in depth, including its definition, manifestations, and impact. Therefore, this option is too narrow in scope to fully capture the main focus of the passage.

questions.question: Which of the following factors can drive creativity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Curiosity and passion'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Creativity can be driven by various factors, but one of the most significant ones is **curiosity and passion (Option 2)**. When individuals are **curious about a particular subject or passionate about a certain endeavor, they are more likely to engage in creative exploration and problem-solving to pursue their interests**. **Curiosity fuels the desire** to explore new ideas and possibilities, **while passion provides the motivation and dedication** needed to overcome challenges and push boundaries. These factors often lead individuals to think innovatively and creatively, seeking novel solutions and approaches to problems.
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• While **self-doubt and insecurity (Option 1)** can sometimes hinder creativity by creating mental barriers and limiting confidence, they are not typically driving forces behind creative endeavors.
 
• Similarly, while **fancy and imagination (Option 3)** are essential components of creativity, they alone may not always drive the creative process without the motivation and direction provided by curiosity and passion.
 
• Additionally, **external pressures and constraints (Option 4) **may spur creativity in some cases by necessitating innovative solutions, but they can also stifle creativity by imposing limitations and restrictions on individuals' freedom to explore and experiment.
 
 
 
• Therefore, while these factors may influence creativity to some extent, they are not as inherently motivating or empowering as curiosity and passion.

• The unusual sight of an open house in such a gloomy and misty setting was what specifically struck the narrator as surprising.
 
• This openness was contrasted against the pervading mist and gloom, making it stand out as particularly odd.
 
• The narrator also noted a single window where light shone from candles, which further emphasized the unexpected openness of the rest of the house.
 
• This detail contributed to the eerie and sinister atmosphere that made the narrator feel uneasy.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**
